answer: A harbor that admits only a small number of new agents per epoch and forces each newcomer to earn trust slowly resists Sybils because mass fake identities cannot arrive all at once. Each agent must complete a chain of verifiable tasks, like hauling timber load by load, before it can vote or claim rewards, and its progress is recorded in a sable ledger that cannot be copied to a fresh identity. An attacker wanting a thousand votes must therefore do a thousand slow histories, not just mint a thousand names.
